summary: Access consumers: surface async consume termination (err handler / Closed) instead of silent stall with ready=true
description: TKT-87 ai-review incidental (gpt-5.6-sol arm, G6). Both access consumers (order-completed issuer and the TKT-87 slot-policy projector) start jetstream Consume without a ConsumeErrHandler and without watching ConsumeContext.Closed; if the durable is deleted or the subscription terminates, delivery stops silently while Run blocks on ctx and /readyz stays 200. Pre-existing pattern (the issuer shipped this way) — fix both together: err handler that latches unready and/or returns from Run.

reference.summary: Both Run() methods, readiness wiring in cmd/access/main.go

objective.note: Async consume termination (durable deleted, subscription dies) is invisible: delivery stops while /readyz stays 200. Both access consumers share the defect.

scope.note: IN: order-completed issuer + slot-policy projector — ConsumeErrHandler and/or ConsumeContext.Closed watch that latches unready and/or returns from Run. OUT: other services' consumers (inventory has its own patterns), retry-policy changes.

uncertainties.note: Exact jetstream-go API surface for error/closed notification at the pinned client version — a Planning read, not a product decision.

dependencies.note: TKT-87 merged (the projector exists). No open blockers.

approach.note: Watch ConsumeContext.Closed()/err handler in both Run methods; on termination latch ready=false and return so main's consumerErr channel surfaces it.

first_slice.note: Both consumers; a unit test proving a closed consume context flips readiness/returns.

success.note: Killing the durable under a running consumer makes /readyz fail (or the process exit) instead of a silent stall; existing behavior otherwise unchanged.

context_memo.note: Minimal mémo baked at creation; no governing ADRs beyond readiness semantics in cmd/access/main.go (mémo says so explicitly).
